entities.summary: Oliver Friggieri was a Maltese poet, novelist, literary critic, and philosopher. He led the establishment of literary history and criticism in Maltese while teaching at the University of Malta, studying the works of Dun Karm, Rużar Briffa, and others. A prolific writer himself, Friggieri explored new genres to advocate the Maltese language, writing the libretti for the first oratorio and the first cantata in Maltese. His work aimed to promote the Maltese cultural identity, while not shying from criticism: one of his most famous novels, Fil-Parlament Ma Jikbrux Fjuri, attacked the tribalistic divisions of society caused by politics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Friggieri's work promoted the Maltese language and cultural identity, contributing to the development of literary history and criticism in Malta. His novels, such as Fil-Parlament Ma Jikbrux Fjuri, addressed social issues like tribalistic divisions, leaving a lasting impact on Maltese literature.
